- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 0.17 negative values in recent days), model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +5% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 3–5% below peak unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish (0.06–0.17), model tends to overestimate mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–4% for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly bullish (e.g., > 0.17 for 3+ days), model often fails to capture downward momentum — reduce forecast by 3–7% for 10+ day horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops in 30d horizon when sentiment is negative — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 10–15 day horizon if sentiment < 0.06.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.17), model overfits short-term noise — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before applying correction.
